newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX treads water after Monday's leap.
newsitem.headline: German DAX treads water after Monday's leap.

text.p: German share prices were treading water on Tuesday, taking a breather after Monday's three percent surge, with traders waiting for the market to consolidate at current levels before pushing prices higher.
Dealers said there was no clear impetus for a further rise today, despite the dollar's climb to over 1.71 marks.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index was trading down 15.64 points at 3,327.13 at 1320 GMT, slightly below the 3,329.76 floor trade close.
But traders were generally positive on the outlook for the market, seeing the DAX now in a trading range of 3,320 to 3,390, with more scope for gains on the upside.
Among stocks in the news, Commerzbank gained 20 pfennigs to 46.30 marks in the bourse session, after sounding a positive note on its outlook for 1997, predicting a further rise in profits.
